MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 22, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 7:10 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Members of the Palos Verdes Youth Basketball League led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Community Development/Public Works Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  City Clerk Heidi Luce
  Administrative Aide Levi Sinkler

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT “RECYCLING HERO” DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE – THIRD QUARTER 2019

  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 14 BRIDLEWOOD CIRCLE
  COMMERCIAL WINNER: THE NORRIS CENTER

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown
  by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-G AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 22, 2019
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 24, 2019

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – OCTOBER 2019

  APPROVED WARRANTS 61989 THROUGH 62109 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $831,445.86; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100119 THROUGH 100519;
  61989 (VOID); 61990 (VOID); 62002 VOID IN THE AMOUNT OF $177,568.69
  FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $1,009,014.55 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT – SEPTEMBER 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT – SEPTEMBER 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION – WORK PERFORMED BY E.C. CONSTRUCTION
  COMPANY FOR THE PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST STORM DRAIN REPAIR
  PROJECT

  ACCEPTED THE PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST STORM DRAIN REPAIR
  PROJECT AS COMPLETE; AUTHORIZED THE CITY CLERK TO FILE A NOTICE
  OF COMPLETION WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGISTRAR-
  RECORDER’S OFFICE ON OCTOBER 23, 2019; AND DIRECTED STAFF TO
  RELEASE THE 5% CONSTRUCTION RETENTION PAYMENT TO E.C.
  CONSTRUCTION IN THE AMOUNT OF $3,020, IF NO CLAIMS ARE FILED
  WITHIN 35 DAYS AFTER RECORDATION.

G.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF OCTOBER 7, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Carmelo Sorce, Cal Water provided a construction update on the Palos Verdes Peninsula Water
Reliability Project.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 22, 2019
 NEW BUSINESS

A.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICERS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached Memorandum of
  Understanding (MOU) between the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District and
  the cities of Rancho Palos Verdes, Rolling Hills, Palos Verdes Estates and Rolling Hills
  Estates for two School Resource Officers.

  City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, City Manager Grammer confirmed the School
  Resource Officers may be deployed to the elementary and middle schools, in addition to
  the high schools.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN regarding the strength of the language
  in the recitals relative to the benefit to the City Rolling Hills Estates, City Attorney Davis
  stated that the MOU provides a sufficient public purpose and protects the City’s interests.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ noted also that one of the high schools is located in the
  City of Rolling Hills Estates.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING (MOU) BETWEEN THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA
  UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT AND THE CITIES OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES,
  ROLLING HILLS, PALOS VERDES ESTATES AND ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  FOR TWO SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICERS AT A COST NOT TO EXCEED
  $19,500 FOR FY 2019-20.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

NONE.

CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE

CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

A.  AGE FRIENDLY REGION – LETTER OF SUPPORT (SBCCOG)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 22, 2019
   Recommendation: That the City Council submit a letter of support to AARP and commit
  to joining the South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) region-wide effort to
  become an “Age-Friendly Region” led by the SBCCOG.

  Community Services Director Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  MAYOR MITCHELL noted that approximately 25% of the City’s population is over the age
  of 65 and there are number of organizations on the Palos Verdes Peninsula working to
  support this population. She believes this commitment would further support those
  efforts.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ and COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also expressed support
  for this type of regional effort.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE SUBMISSION OF A LETTER OF
  SUPPORT TO AARP AND A COMMITMENT TO JOIN THE SOUTH BAY CITIES
  COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS (SBCCOG) REGION-WIDE EFFORT TO
  BECOME AN “AGE-FRIENDLY REGION”

  There being no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

OTHER CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the SBCCOG will be relocating its offices early next year
to a location near the intersection of Sepulveda Blvd. and Crenshaw Blvd. and staff will be
temporarily dislocated between November and January while the new building is being made ready
for occupancy. She also reported that the SBCCOG Legislative Breakfast held on October 10 was
very informative and successful.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the Holiday Parade Subcommittee met on Monday to
discuss the parade grand marshals. She noted that “Citizens of the Year” Pam Barret-Hill and Jim
Hill will be the Community Grand Marshals and other individuals are still under consideration for
the remaining grand marshal positions.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported that the SCAG Community, Economic and Human
Development (CEHD) Committee met this week to discuss its recommendation to the Regional
Council regarding the proposed RHNA methodology. He also reported that a subcommittee was
created to evaluate and respond to the State’s response to SCAG’s letter regarding the allocation
methodology, and he will serve on that subcommittee.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that the City of Westlake Village recently joined the
Clean Power Alliance, but no additional cities will be added until 2020 with a one year delay for
participation.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 22, 2019
 MAYOR MITCHELL reported that several members of the City Council and staff attended last
week’s League of California Cites Annual Conference and Expo which provided many networking
and learning opportunities.

MAYOR MITCHELL also reported that she recently visited and toured CARB’s new Laboratory
Facility in Riverside where it certifies vehicles for emission standards. She further reported that she
attended an informative transportation conference focused on environmental justice organized by
the Institute for Transportation Studies.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER):

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future
  consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  REDUCING CRIME AND KEEPING CALIFORNIA SAFE ACT OF 2020 (MAYOR
  MITCHELL)

  MAYOR MITCHELL stated that she received a letter from the Mayor of Whittier requesting
  the City’s support of the Keeping California Safe Act of 2020 which fixes some of the flaws
  contained in AB 109 and Propositions 47 and 57.

  Discussion ensued concerning the purpose of the Keeping California Safe Act of 2020 and
  the merits of supporting the Act.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL SUPPORT THE REDUCING CRIME AND KEEPING
  CALIFORNIA SAFE ACT OF 2020.

  There being no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

B.  COX COMMUNICATIONS PENINSULA WIDE TOWN HALL MEETING (VERBAL
  REPORT)

  City Manager Grammer reported that the City was contacted by the City of Palos Verdes
  Estates to see if there was interest in co-hosting a public forum with Cox Communications
  to provide Cox an opportunity to talk with residents about their services, programs and
  improvements and to respond to the concerns and questions resident have had. He stated
  that staff is reaching out to the other cities to determine their interest and working on securing
  the Norris Pavilion for the event.

  COUNCIL expressed support for staff’s efforts in this regard.

OTHER MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF encouraged Council and residents to attend the Prepared Peninsula
Expo this Sunday, October 27 from noon to 3:00 pm at the Norris Pavilion.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 22, 2019
 CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Davis stated that staff proposes to add one matter of significant exposure to litigation
under Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) to the agenda as permitted under the Brown Act
with a 4/5 vote of the COUNCIL.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL add the following item to the closed session agenda:
  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant Exposure to Litigation: One potential case

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Potential Initiation of Litigation: Two potential cases

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant Exposure to Litigation: One potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

ADJOURNMENT

At 8:21 p.m. MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the open session portion of the City Council meeting
in memory of long-time resident and Equestrian Committee member Carol Dean-Porter and the
City Council recessed into closed session in the Conference Room at City Hall.

At 9:10 p.m. MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned closed session portion of the City Council meeting.
The next regular City Council meeting is scheduled to be held on Tuesday, November 12, 2019
at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive
North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 22, 2019
